passage: Temperature is a physical quantity that expresses the degree of hotness or coldness of a substance. The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin (K). In everyday life, temperature is commonly measured in degrees Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F). Absolute zero is 0 K or -273.15 °C. Heat is energy in transit that flows from a higher temperature body to a lower temperature body until thermal equilibrium is reached.
